page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6v-c8g1.16xlarge is a GPU-accelerated server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 64 vCPUs and 32 physical cores utilizing the Intel Xeon 8163 processor on the x86_64 architecture, running at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB per core. Acceleration is driven by eight NVIDIA Volta V100 GPUs, delivering a total of 128 GB of VRAM. No local storage is bundled with this instance, requiring reliance on network-attached storage, while network connectivity is supported by a 20 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance dichotomy between single-core and multi-core operations. Single-threaded performance is relatively weak, with stress-ng single-core scoring in the bottom 25% and single-threaded gzip compression registering in the bottom 10%. Conversely, multi-threaded capabilities are robust; the instance achieves a strong top 25% rating in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and an average rating in multi-core stress-ng CPU performance. Memory bandwidth is stable, with large-block read and write speeds averaging 121.44 GB/sec and 48.0 GB/sec respectively. Redis SET operations reach 41.84 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput is measured at 24.7 GB/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this instance represents a high-density hardware profile where the primary value resides in its massive parallel GPU capabilities rather than single-core CPU efficiency. The lack of local storage means storage costs must be factored in separately. Given the eight NVIDIA V100 GPUs and strong multi-threaded decompression performance, this server is best suited for GPU-accelerated workloads such as deep learning training, parallel scientific computing, and complex multi-threaded data processing, rather than single-threaded application hosting.
